edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 9

source_text: Sinistra eius sub capite meo, et dextera eius complexabitur me. Habet et sinistram et dexteram Sermo Dei. Sapientia, cum pro intellectus varietate se praebet, nunc sinistra, nunc dextera dicitur. Sinistra temporalium et corporalium cura; dextera aeternorum et spiritalium donatio. Sub capite sinistra: ne mens circa temporalia evagetur, sed subiecta sit. Dextera complexatur: aeterna amplectitur et custodit.
pass_a_gloss: Left-hand of-him under my head, and right-hand of-him will-embrace me. He-has both left and right Word of-God. Wisdom when for variety of-understanding herself she-offers, now left now right is-called. Left of-temporal and bodily care; right of-eternal and spiritual gift. Under head left: lest mind about temporals wander but be subject. Right embraces: eternals clasps and keeps.
pass_b_english: [[His left hand is under my head, and his right hand will embrace me >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:6]]. The Word of God has both a left hand and a right. Wisdom, when she offers herself according to the variety of understanding, is called now left, now right. The left is care for temporal and bodily things; the right is the gift of eternal and spiritual things. The left under the head: lest the mind wander about temporal things, but be subject. The right embraces: it clasps and keeps eternal things.
notes: Song Homilia II OET; Lawson not used for wording.
